subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should this issue remain the focused current-PID restart/recovery lock tracker, or should maintainers move the remaining live current-PID lock behavior to a broader session-lock issue after acknowledging the shipped partial fix?
rationale: Source inspection shows the original boot/untracked-self cleanup is partly implemented, but reclaiming a lock owned by the live gateway crosses a transcript data-integrity boundary that automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and max-hold subcases.

options.title: Move To Broader Tracker
options.body: Close only after explicitly linking the remaining live current-PID behavior to a canonical open issue such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86538 and preserving the field evidence there.

options.title: Declare Boot Cleanup Complete
options.body: Treat the original boot-sweep request as done by the shipped untracked-self cleanup and open a narrower follow-up for runtime/recovery live current-PID leaks.

recommendation.title: Keep Focused Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and max-hold subcases.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on session-write-lock hardening and the gateway/session-lock policy boundary.
